blocks.prompt: 1. Let us make paratha roll. We can choose our fillings from the following: Meat: Chicken or beef; Vegetable: Onions, tomatoes or cucumber; Sauce: Mayo or Chutney. How many different kinds of rolls can we make?
blocks.explanation:
A roll is made in three independent stages: choose a meat, choose a vegetable, choose a sauce.
We must count all the different rolls.
Plan: count the options at each stage and multiply them (Fundamental Principle of Counting).
steps:
Given: meat: 2 options (chicken, beef); vegetable: 3 options (onions, tomatoes, cucumber); sauce: 2 options (mayo, chutney).
To find: the number of different kinds of rolls.
Method: Fundamental Principle of Counting: if independent choices can be made in \(m\), \(n\) and \(p\) ways, all of them together can be made in \(m \times n \times p\) ways.

Count the choices at each stage
\[\text{meat} = 2,\quad \text{vegetable} = 3\]
\[\text{sauce} = 2\]
Why: One filling is taken from each group, and choosing one does not change the options in the other groups, so the stages are independent.

Multiply the choices
\[\text{rolls} = 2 \times 3 \times 2\]
\[= 6 \times 2 = 12\]
Why: Each of the 2 meats can go with each of the 3 vegetables (6 pairs), and each pair can take either of the 2 sauces.

Check by listing one branch
\[\text{Chicken: } 3 \times 2 = 6 \text{ rolls}\]
\[\text{Beef: } 3 \times 2 = 6 \text{ rolls}\]
\[6 + 6 = 12 \;\checkmark\]
Why: For chicken the rolls are onion-mayo, onion-chutney, tomato-mayo, tomato-chutney, cucumber-mayo, cucumber-chutney; beef gives the same 6 again.
